paragraphs: An astonishing story is told about something that also happened to him through R-M [ר״מ]. Seder HaDorot copied it from a small book of stories, so Hyman sees no need to repeat it.

notes.text: The person abbreviated ר״מ is not identified. The phrase מס׳ קטן מעשיות is read as a small book of stories; Hyman is the one declining to repeat it.

The saved whole Warsaw1878–1882 Seder HaDorot1644:1 tells the story under abbreviated R' Yehudah HaAnatoti and itself repeatedly uses ר״מ. It supplies no full-title expansion or explicit Meir name for these occurrences, so the heading remains R' and R-M stays unexpanded. Rabbi Meir is only a conventional proposed expansion. The source booklet was not traced; the final ס' קטן מעשיות does not identify an edition or settle the small-book interpretation. Hyman declines to repeat the narrative; none of that omitted tale is imported.

Seder HaDorot 1644:1 gives the story and uses the initials R-M. Hyman refers back to this story in his own article on Rabbi Meir (vol. III, p. 874). The version in the Mimkor Yisrael folklore database also names Rabbi Meir. The specific edition of the small book cited by Seder HaDorot has yet to be identified.
